name: ML-Driven Surrogate Modeling for Airfoil Design
description: Develop machine learning models to predict steady-state 2D velocity and pressure fields around airfoils, compute aerodynamic properties, and optimize lift-over-drag ratios while ensuring physical consistency and generalization to out-of-distribution scenarios.

cr:input.name: competition_dataset
cr:input.description: Participants receive point cloud data representing the simulation mesh, including node positions, inlet velocity, distance to the airfoil, normals, and the airfoil geometry as an unstructured mesh. For example, a sample input may include numerical arrays for node positions and inlet velocity, along with mesh data representing the airfoil geometry.

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: Predictions include numerical values for physical fields (ux, uy, p, νt, ps) and derived quantities (CL, CD, ρD, ρL). Values must adhere to physical consistency and calibrated thresholds for evaluation.

field.name: id
field.description: unique identifier for the sample, e.g., airfoil_001

field.name: ux
field.description: predicted velocity component in the x direction

field.name: uy
field.description: predicted velocity component in the y direction

field.name: ps
field.description: predicted pressure divided by specific mass

cr:evaluation.notes: The global score is a weighted linear combination of ML-related metrics (40%), physics compliance metrics (30%), and OOD generalization metrics (30%). Accuracy scores are calibrated with thresholds, and speedup is normalized to a maximum score of 1.
